I checked the code: Extract log's success notification already names the destination note and section. So the request is already partly met. I can't write firm requirements until the owner says what's missing (Q1 below).

## What the code does now (answers the owner's reply)

- **Success notice.** After the target note is written and the source is updated, it shows `Extract log: moved child block to "<target basename>" > <section text>` for 4 seconds (`src/commands/extractLog.ts:168-171`, `src/config.ts:15`).
  - The note is shown by its file name only (no folder or `.md`), in quotes.
  - The section is the configured log heading (default `## Log`) with the `#`s removed, so you see `Log` (`extractLog.ts:116`, `src/utils/tasks.ts:20-31`).
- **What the notice leaves out:**
  - The new dated sub-heading the content actually goes under, e.g. `### [[2026-11-09 Mon]] Checkin mit Chris` (`extractLog.ts:117-119`, inserted at `:158-160`).
  - Whether the `## Log` section already existed or was just added at the end of the file (`tasks.ts:253-271`).
  - The note's folder. Two notes with the same name look identical.
  - That the content was also copied to the clipboard. That copy happens silently and fails silently (`extractLog.ts:17-29`, `:72-75`).
  - It is plain text with no link to click.
- **Other notices:**
  - "No children" (`extractLog.ts:63`)
  - "No listItems metadata" (`extractLog.ts:57`)
  - "No wikilink found" (`extractLog.ts:109`)
  - A catch-all error shown for 8 seconds (`extractLog.ts:173-176`, `config.ts:20`)
- **Tests.** Nothing checks the success notice's text. The integration tests only check the "No children" and error notices (`tests/integration/extractLog.plugin.test.ts:43,362`). The test helper does record every notice (`tests/helpers/extractLogPluginTestHelper.ts:170-206`).
- **Similar command.** Complete project task's notice uses wikilink style: `Task completed and logged to [[Migration Initiative]].` (`tests/integration/completeProjectTask.plugin.test.ts:329-331`).

## Intended outcome (requirement)
After a successful Extract log, the notification tells the user where the content went, clearly enough that they don't need to open the target note to check.

## Questions that block progress
1. **What's missing from today's notice?** It already names the note and section. Which of these should be added?
   a. The dated sub-heading, e.g. `"Migration Initiative" > Log > [[2026-11-09 Mon]] Checkin mit Chris`
   b. The folder or full path, so same-named notes can be told apart
   c. A note when the Log section was just created
   d. That the content was copied to the clipboard
   e. A clickable link to the new spot
   f. Only rewording (for example, matching Complete project task's `[[Note]]` style)
   Also: could the user be on an older version that doesn't show this notice yet?
2. **If (e) is wanted:** a clickable notice adds UI behaviour and needs Obsidian code in `src/adapters/`. Is that in scope, or should the notice stay plain text?
3. **Should the notice stay visible longer than 4 seconds?** That's the shared success timeout, so changing it for every command is a separate decision.

## Assumptions (please confirm or correct)
- Only the wording or content of the success notice changes. Where content is inserted, the source link rewrite and the error notices stay the same.
- The notice is still shown only after both the target note and the source note have been updated.
- Users don't need a new setting for this.

## Acceptance cases (draft, to fill in once Q1 is answered)
- **Named link.** Extracting from `- Checkin mit Chris zu [[Migration Initiative]]` with children gives a notice naming `Migration Initiative`, the Log section, and whatever extra detail Q1 picks.
- **Bare link bullet.** For a bullet that's only a link (`- [[Project]]`), the notice reflects the heading built from the parent bullet.
- **Missing Log section.** If the target note has no Log section, the notice is accurate, and says the section was created if Q1(c) is chosen.
- **Custom heading.** With the log heading set to `### Inbox`, the notice says `Inbox`.
- **Unchanged cases.** No children → "No children" notice and no notice naming a destination. A failed write → error notice only.

## High-level plan
1. Write integration tests first that pin the exact success text in `tests/integration/extractLog.plugin.test.ts`, using the helper's `notice` field.
2. Move the message building into a pure helper in `src/utils/notices.ts`, next to `formatTransferNotice`, with unit tests. Its inputs would be the note name, section text, and the optional details chosen in Q1.
3. Call that helper from `extractLog.ts:168`. If the "section created" detail is wanted, `insertBlockAfterHeading` would need to report that back.
4. Add a CHANGELOG entry written from the user's point of view.

# Requirements handoff (revision 3): ticking a task in a weekly, monthly or yearly note cascades it down to today's daily Log

## Intended outcome
You tick a task `[x]` in a weekly, monthly or yearly note. The task then moves down one level at a time until it reaches today's daily note, where it ends up completed under `dailyNoteLogHeading` (default `## Log`). Every note it passes through keeps it as `[<]`. After this, weekly, monthly and yearly notes never hold a completed task, and the `[<]` markers plus wikilinks are the paper trail.

## What the latest reply settled
- **Q1 (in-between notes) → yes.** Each in-between note (this month, this week) gets a real copy under `periodicNoteTaskTargetHeading` (`## Todo`), which is then marked `[<]`. That's the same result as running push task down twice by hand.
- **Q2 (a matching task already in an in-between note) → (a), merge the way push down does.** Push down merges with `insertMultipleTasksWithDeduplication` (`src/utils/tasks.ts:612-638`). It reopens a matching `[<]` task and nests the incoming children under it (`tasks.ts:575-594`). In a cascade, the merged task, including the children it already had, carries on down and is marked `[<]`.
- **Implementation preference.** Extend and reuse the push-down code rather than writing a parallel path.

The earlier answers still hold. The push cascades instead of skipping levels. If today isn't inside the source note's period, nothing moves and a notice appears. A ticked subtask moves on its own. A project task is logged in the project note under a link back to the daily note.

## Firm requirements
1. The trigger is a change *to* `[x]` in a weekly, monthly or yearly note, in any section.
2. The source line becomes `[<]` and is not deleted.
3. Each in-between note gets the task under its Todo heading as `[<]`, merging with a matching task if there is one.
4. Today's daily note gets the task as `[x]` under `dailyNoteLogHeading`.
5. If today isn't inside the source period, nothing moves, the line stays `[x]` and a notice appears. This matches push down (`src/commands/pushTaskDown.ts:73-77`).
6. A ticked subtask moves alone; its parent stays open.
7. A project task gets one entry in the project log, under the daily note's link.
8. Daily notes behave exactly as they do now (`src/events/autoMoveCompleted.ts:169`).

## Remaining question (it only blocks acceptance case 13)
- **A matching task already in today's daily note.** Daily Log insertion doesn't deduplicate today. So if today's Todo already holds an open `- [ ] Call Sam`, you'd end up with `[ ]` in Todo and `[x]` in Log. Options:
  - (a) Allow the duplicate.
  - (b) Merge the way the in-between notes do, so the existing task is completed and moved to Log.
  - Unless you say otherwise, I'll assume (a), because it's the smallest change.

## Assumptions (not confirmed; please correct any that are wrong)
- **A1.** It runs automatically in the existing tick handler, with no new command. The "Complete project task" command counts as a tick.
- **A2.** Setting `[/]` in a non-daily note does nothing. That differs from daily Todo, where started tasks also move (`autoMoveCompleted.ts:190`). Editing a line that is already `[<]`, `[>]` or `[x]` doesn't trigger anything.
- **A3.** Children follow push-down rules. Open children move with the task; completed subtrees stay in the source (`pushTaskDown.ts:140-141`, `175-180`).
- **A4.** For a project task, the children go to the project log and only the task line lands in the daily Log. That mirrors `moveLineOnly` (`autoMoveCompleted.ts:203-215`).
- **A5.** Missing in-between notes, a missing daily note and missing headings are created (`getOrCreateFile`, `pushTaskDown.ts:93`).
- **A6.** Writes go from the bottom up: the daily note and project note first, then the in-between notes, then the source. The source edit comes last, after checking the line hasn't changed. If a write fails, the source stays `[x]` and an error notice appears. Notes already written are not rolled back.
- **A7.** Unticking afterwards doesn't undo anything.

## Acceptance cases
| # | Given | When | Then |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | This week's note: `- [ ] Call Sam` | tick it | weekly `- [<] Call Sam`; daily Log `- [x] Call Sam` |
| 2 | This month's note | tick a task | monthly `[<]`; week Todo `[<]`; daily Log `[x]` |
| 3 | This year's note | tick a task | yearly, month and week all `[<]`; daily Log `[x]` |
| 4 | Last week's note, or next month's | tick a task | stays `[x]`; notice shown; no other note changes |
| 5 | Subtask under an open parent | tick the subtask | the subtask cascades; the parent stays `[ ]` |
| 6 | Task with one open child and one completed child | tick it | the open child travels; the completed child stays under the `[<]` line |
| 7 | `[[Project]] Draft memo` in the weekly note | tick it | weekly `[<]`; daily Log `[x]`; one project-log entry under the daily note's link |
| 8 | Today's daily note or this week's note doesn't exist | tick in the monthly note | the missing notes are created and the cascade completes |
| 9 | Weekly note | set `[/]` | nothing happens |
| 10 | Daily note | tick a task in Todo | same as today |
| 11 | Writing to the daily note fails | tick in the weekly note | source stays `[x]`; error notice shown |
| 12 | This week already has `- [<] Call Sam` with one child | tick `Call Sam` in the monthly note | the week has one `Call Sam` line, `[<]`, holding both sets of children; the daily Log gets `[x]` with the open children |
| 13 | Today's Todo already has `- [ ] Call Sam` | tick it in the weekly note | depends on the remaining question |

## Implementation plan (high level, reusing push down as asked)
1. **Pull the core of `pushTaskDown` into a reusable step (unit tests first).** It would take a task and its transferable children and work on text instead of the editor. It would do what push down does now: prepare the content (`prepareTaskContentForTarget`), route it to the target (`routeTaskInsert`, `insertMultipleTasksWithDeduplication` / `insertProjectTasksInSection`), and mark the source (`markTaskAsScheduled`).
   - The step also needs to say where the task landed (inserted or merged), so the next hop can pick that subtree up and mark it `[<]`. The current insert functions only return counts (`tasks.ts:612-638`).
   - The `pushTaskDown` command then becomes one call to this step, with its behaviour unchanged.
2. **Cascade.** Starting from the source note, call `getLowerNotePath` (`periodicNotes.ts`) and the shared step over and over until the target is the daily note. The last hop goes into the daily Log as `[x]`, using `findLogInsertionLine` and the heading-creation branch of `computeAutoMove` (`src/utils/autoMove.ts:95`, `:189`).
3. **Routing in `runAutoMove`.** Replace the daily-only check at `autoMoveCompleted.ts:169`. Daily notes keep the current path. Other periodic notes first check `dateIsInPeriod`, then write from the bottom up with `vault.process`, then edit the source after the re-read check. Project tasks reuse the project-completion adapter, with the daily note as the link source.
4. **Integration tests** for every case above, following `tests/CLAUDE.md`. Keep the existing push-down tests green to show the refactor didn't change that command.
5. **Docs.** Add a CHANGELOG line ("Ticking a task in a weekly, monthly or yearly note files it down to today's daily log"). Update the heading-settings table in CLAUDE.md and the header comment in `autoMoveCompleted.ts`.
